## Week of August 10

Product Update Now Available: Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B from Alibaba Cloud

Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, a 2.4 trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model built for long-context and agentic workloads, is now available on DigitalOcean Inference Engine.

...

- Massive context window: Processes up to 1M tokens, enabling full-codebase or large-document-set reasoning in a single pass.
- Strong agentic and coding performance: On Alibaba Cloud’s published benchmarks, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B leads PaperBench (93.0) and IFBench (82.8), and scores 86.6 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 — ahead of Claude Opus 4.8/Fable 5 (84.6), though behind GPT-5.6 Sol (88.8) and trailing on SWE-bench Pro (67.7 vs. Fable 5’s 80.0).
- Lower list price: $2/$6 per 1M tokens (input/output), versus Claude Fable 5’s $10/$50.
- Optimized inference infrastructure: Launching on NVIDIA HGX™ B300 GPUs using NVFP4-quantized weights, developed through a technical collaboration with Inferact to tune performance for this model on DigitalOcean’s infrastructure.

Start using Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B through the DigitalOcean API or directly in the Cloud Console. See the product docs for details.

Product Update Introducing Spot GPU Droplets (Public Preview)

The latest generation of GPUs is in high demand, making it challenging for developers and AI teams to access capacity for short-lived workloads that don’t require long-running GPU reservations. Starting today, Spot GPU Droplets are available in Public Preview, giving customers access to the latest-generation NVIDIA HGX™B300 and AMD Instinct™ MI350X/MI355X GPUs at a Spot price locked at creation for the life of the Droplet. Spot GPU Droplets are interruptible and can be reclaimed at any time. We aim to give at least two hours’ notice by email, enough time to checkpoint your jobs so they can resume later. Spot is a strong fit for experimentation, batch training, batch inference, and rendering.

Spot GPU Droplets are available in Public Preview in RIC1, MKC1, ATL1, and MEM1. The preview includes NVIDIA HGX™ B300 and AMD Instinct™ MI350X/MI355X GPUs, with additional GPU types, regions, and available capacity planned over time based on customer feedback.

To learn more about Spot GPU Droplets, including supported GPU types, interruption behavior, and best practices, see our product documentation.

For pricing information, visit the GPU Droplets pricing page.

To get started, launch your first Spot GPU Droplet from the DigitalOcean console.

For the terms and conditions that apply to Spot GPU Droplets, visit the Preview Terms.

AI applications spend most of their compute budget re-sending the same context on every request: system prompts, tool definitions, retrieved documents, conversation history. With Prompt Caching, DigitalOcean automatically recognizes repeated token prefixes and currently offers an 80% discount on cached input tokens compared to standard input pricing across supported models. See the pricing page for current rates, applicable terms, and any pricing updates. The result is lower costs and faster time-to-first-token, with no changes to your application code. Caching applies automatically, and every API response includes a `cached_tokens` count so you can verify your savings in real time. It is available today across a broad set of leading open models, with more models coming soon.

# 7 Replicate Alternatives for AI Inference in 2027

By Maddy Osman

- Costs that are hard to forecast: Per-second and per-output billing shifts with GPU tier, run length, and queue backlog, so you can’t budget confidently until you’ve seen real traffic. DigitalOcean GPU Droplets bill at a published hourly rate, and a 12-month reservation locks that rate in, so your GPU compute cost is a known number to plan around.
- Cold starts on interactive features: A model that hasn’t run recently must boot a container and load weights before it can respond. GPUs that stay provisioned avoid that delay during regular use.
- Paying for idle time on custom models: When deploying your own model, Replicate runs it on dedicated hardware and bills setup, idle, and active time—it’s not as simple as paying only for what you use.
- Dependence on another company’s roadmap: Replicate now sits inside Cloudflare. As with any acquisition, a platform’s roadmap is set by its new owner, which is something we think is worth weighing on a multi-year commitment. Running containers on infrastructure you operate directly keeps those decisions in your hands, and Cog’s standard Docker packaging keeps the move itself manageable.
- Outgrowing a single endpoint: A prototype on one model endpoint often has to change platforms once you require multi-GPU capacity or model routing. On DigitalOcean, you can start on one GPU Droplet, move the same container to a Bare Metal cluster, and add Inference Engine for routing, all without re-platforming.

...

### Dedicated GPU infrastructure

Dedicated infrastructure runs on hardware the provider operates directly, so GPUs stay provisioned and billing follows a known hourly rate instead of per-request metering.

#### DigitalOcean for production inference on dedicated, always-on GPUs

 DigitalOcean is the AI-Native Cloud, offering dedicated GPU compute alongside a managed inference layer—the structural alternative to Replicate’s marketplace model. Rather than brokering someone else’s compute, DigitalOcean runs the infrastructure directly through GPU Droplets and Bare Metal GPUs. Teams running on DigitalOcean have always-on GPU access at a flat, transparent rate for your chosen commitment tier. Because the GPUs stay provisioned, requests do not wait for a container boot once the model is loaded. The Inference Engine adds an endpoint compatible with the OpenAI and Anthropic API formats, plus policy-driven routing to choose which model handles a request based on rules like cost, latency, or availability. Use it across 70+ open and frontier models, while the AI Platform layers in Managed Agents and data tooling for teams building full AI applications rather than just calling a model. For a workload running on Replicate, that combination addresses its two biggest pain points: unpredictable cost and infrastructure you don’t control.

DigitalOcean key features:

- Always-on GPU Droplets and Bare Metal GPUs run on hardware DigitalOcean operates, so models stay warm between requests.
- Inference Engine provides one OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible endpoint with policy-driven routing by cost, latency, or availability across 70+ open and frontier models.
- AI Platform adds managed agents, knowledge bases, and data tooling on the same infrastructure.

DigitalOcean pricing:

- GPU Droplets (H100): $4.41/hour on-demand; $3.26/hour with a 12-month reservation.
- Bare Metal GPUs: dedicated, single-tenant H100/H200/MI300X servers, provisioned by contract.
- Inference Engine and AI Platform: usage-based pricing.

...

Which inference provider offers predictable costs without surprise bills?

Dedicated GPU infrastructure with flat or reserved pricing is the most predictable option, because the rate doesn’t change based on how a single run behaves. DigitalOcean GPU Droplets cost $4.41 an hour on-demand for an H100, or $3.26 an hour with a 12-month reservation. With per-second billing, by contrast, the cost of a given workload depends on run length, GPU tier, and queue depth, which makes spend harder to forecast before you have seen real production traffic.

highlights:
# What Is DigitalOcean? Inside the AI-Native Cloud (2027)

By Jesse Sumrak

Sr. Content Marketing Manager

- Updated: November 3, 2026
- 11 min read

...

### Infrastructure

GPU Droplets and Bare Metal GPUs provide NVIDIA and AMD accelerators for training, fine-tuning, and dedicated inference (billed per second on demand).

DigitalOcean owns the GPUs it runs, rather than reselling third-party capacity, so GPU pricing is not subject to a reseller markup. Actual costs vary by configuration, region, and workload.

The infrastructure layer includes:

- 20 data centers across 13 regions, with air-cooled and liquid-cooled infrastructure
- NVIDIA H100, H200, and HGX B300 GPUs
- AMD Instinct MI300X, MI325X, MI350X, and MI355X GPUs
- 400G RoCE fabric for high-bandwidth, low-latency GPU-to-GPU networking

...

Inference Engine’s three modes match your workload to the most appropriate pricing model:

- Serverless inference for real-time apps and agents, billed per token.
- Dedicated inference for steady, high-volume traffic or custom models, billed per GPU-hour.
- Batch inference for asynchronous jobs, priced at a discount of up to 50% off real-time rates on supported models, with a target completion window of 24 hours.

...

Inference Router is in Public Preview: it is offered without a service level agreement, features may change or be withdrawn, and preview pricing, including the current no-routing-fee pricing, may change at general availability. See the Preview Terms.

...

## DigitalOcean’s predictable pricing and billing

Cloud pricing is infamously tricky to forecast, and AI only makes it harder. You’ll often find token rates, GPU-hours, storage, and data transfer coming from several invoices from different vendors, and the total almost never matches the estimate.

DigitalOcean keeps pricing simple and transparent with an all-in-one bill. Rates below are in USD, exclude applicable taxes, and are subject to change; Public Preview pricing may change at general availability. See the pricing page for current rates:

- Serverless inference: From about $0.05 per million tokens, depending on the model.
- Dedicated inference: From $2.59 per GPU-hour (AMD Instinct MI300X), depending on GPU type and configuration.
- Batch inference: Up to 50% off real-time rates on supported OpenAI and Anthropic models.
- Harness Runtime: $0.044 per vCPU-hour and $0.0095 per GB-hour, billed per second. An idle agent’s CPU charge drops to zero.
- Action Gateway: $0.10 per 1,000 standard tool calls, with tool search included.
- App Platform: From $5 per month for a container, with a free tier for static sites.
- Managed Databases: PostgreSQL from $15.15 per month.
- Inference Router: No separate routing fee. You pay only for the model that serves each request.

Routing lowers costs by sending simpler requests to cheaper models.

Inference, GPU Droplets, Kubernetes, databases, and storage are all on the same invoice. This lets you reliably estimate the entire stack in advance using the DigitalOcean pricing calculator. Running everything on one network also means traffic between your app, database, and models doesn’t have to cross clouds, which can reduce data transfer charges.

Where a stack spans multiple providers, charges such as cross-cloud data transfer can be harder to forecast. Compare each provider’s published rates for your own configuration.

Pricing and feature information reflects publicly available documentation as of October 2026 and may vary by region and workload. For the most current pricing and availability, refer to each provider’s official documentation.

| Point of comparison | DigitalOcean | Baseten |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Company background | Publicly traded (NYSE: DOCN); AI-Native Cloud built on existing GPU Droplets, managed databases, and networking; CEO Paddy Srinivasan. | Independent inference and training platform built around dedicated, single-tenant GPU deployments; founded 2019 by repeat founders Tuhin Srivastava and Philip Howes. |
| Model catalog | 70+ open/multimodal models hosted directly, plus proxied OpenAI/Anthropic access with day-zero availability on top new releases. | Open-weight models only (including Llama, DeepSeek, Qwen, and GPT-OSS) across Model APIs and dedicated deployments—no GPT or Claude. |
| Deployment type | Serverless Inference (pay-per-token) for standard workloads; dedicated GPU Droplets (per-second) for single-tenant control. | Model APIs (per-token, open models) plus dedicated deployments billed continuously per GPU-minute per replica, with scale-to-zero as the default. |
| Pricing model | Serverless ~$0.10–$1.05+/1M input tokens; dedicated GPU-hour from $2.59; batch up to 50% off OpenAI/Anthropic; one bill across inference, databases, storage, compute. | Dedicated GPU from ~$4.00/hr (A100) to ~$9.98/hr (B200), billed per minute per replica; Model APIs from ~$0.10/1M tokens. |
| Reliability | Inference Router (public preview, all accounts) can reroute to a fallback model when the selected model is down or rate limited. | 99.99% marketed uptime; 99.95% SLA on Enterprise’s Mission Critical tier. |
| Security & compliance | SOC 2 Type II and SOC 3 Type II compliance certification; Zero Data Retention by default; VPC-on-serverless; HIPAA-eligible on select Covered Products via BAA. | SOC 2 Type II and PCI DSS attestations; states HIPAA and GDPR readiness; Zero Data Retention by default for synchronous inference. |
| Support | 24/7 support included on every account; paid tiers add faster response and dedicated account management. | Support response times not publicly published as of October 2026 (email and in-app chat on Basic; Slack and Zoom on Pro; custom SLAs on Enterprise).

...

## Pricing

Billing model is where DigitalOcean vs Baseten diverge most, and it’s the detail most worth running your own numbers against before committing.

Here’s how each actually charges for GPU capacity:

| | DigitalOcean | Baseten |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Serverless/Model APIs tokens | ~$0.10–$1.05+ per 1M input tokens for DigitalOcean-hosted models; proxied OpenAI/Anthropic bill at each provider’s list rates | ~$0.10 per 1M tokens on comparable open models |
| Dedicated inference | From $2.59/GPU-hour (AMD MI300X) | ~$4.00/hr (A100) to ~$9.98/hr (B200), billed per minute per replica, continuously while the replica is up |
| Redundancy cost | No replica floor for standard inference; dedicated GPU Droplets bill per second only while running | Running a second replica for high availability roughly doubles the dedicated-deployment bill—without doubling throughput |
| Enterprise/Pro pricing | Published rate cards for every tier | Not published; requires a sales conversation |
| Billing structure | One bill across inference, databases, storage, and compute | Per-replica-minute and per-token billing, separate from any other infrastructure a team runs elsewhere—plus cross-cloud egress if data moves between them |

Baseten’s dedicated deployments bill per GPU-minute per replica. At its published rate of $0.10833/minute for an H100 80GB (as of October 2026), a single always-on replica running 24/7 for a 30-day month costs about $4,680, assuming no commit or volume discount, regardless of how much traffic it serves. Baseten’s autoscaling documentation recommends min_replica: 1 “as a starting point when you need to avoid scale-from-zero latency” and at least two “when you also need replica redundancy” (accessed October 2026).

...

The DigitalOcean Inference Engine is pay-per-token for standard workloads, with no replica floor to manage, and operates next to dedicated GPU Droplets for teams that specifically need single-tenant control. A steady, high-throughput workload can still land at a lower cost per request on Baseten’s dedicated tier than on serverless pricing—which is exactly why the redundancy math is worth running before committing. After all, paying for standby capacity around the clock is a real cost, not a rounding error, once a workload needs high availability.

highlights:
By Shridhar Pandey

- Updated: October 9, 2026

...

## Pricing

You only pay for compute usage while a MicroVM is running, at $0.022 per vCPU-hour and $0.0085 per GiB-hour, billed per second. Storage, billed at $0.05 per GiB-month on what you actually use, keeps each MicroVM’s disk and saved state available, so a paused MicroVM costs you only for its storage. Outbound data transfer on public networking is $0.01 per GiB.

| Resource | Rate |
| --- | --- |
| vCPU | $0.022 per vCPU-hour |
| Memory | $0.0085 per GiB-hour |
| Storage | $0.05 per GiB-month |

A MicroVM allocated 2 vCPU and 4 GiB memory, if run for a full hour, will cost $0.078 in compute usage. A coding-agent session with this vCPU and memory configuration, that runs for 15 minutes in that hour and is paused the rest of the time, will only cost $0.0195 in compute, plus the storage it uses. So, the longer a session is idle, the less you spend on compute.
